answer_text:
# 🎮 Best Free 3D Game Assets (2026)

Here's a comprehensive guide to the best websites and sources for free 3D game assets:

---

## 🏆 Top Websites for Free 3D Game Assets

### 1. 🌟 [Kenney.nl](https://kenney.nl)
This one-person operation has released over **40,000 assets** — all CC0, all free, no sign-up required. The art style is clean, colourful, and remarkably consistent across packs, meaning you can mix and match assets easily. The site offers 2D assets, 3D models, UI elements, fonts, and audio.
- ✅ **License:** CC0 (Public Domain) — No attribution needed
- 🎯 **Best for:** Rapid prototyping, stylized games, UI elements

---

### 2. 🎨 [Quaternius](https://quaternius.com)
If you're making a 3D game with a stylised low-poly look, Quaternius is essential. This artist has released thousands of models — characters, animals, vehicles, environments, weapons — all under CC0. The signature "Quaternius style" is instantly recognisable: clean geometry, bright colours, charming animations. Assets come rigged and animated, ready to drop into Unity, Unreal, or Godot.
- ✅ **License:** CC0 (Public Domain)
- 🎯 **Best for:** Low-poly 3D games, animated characters

---

### 3. 🖼️ [Poly Haven](https://polyhaven.com)
Poly Haven started as HDRI Haven and has grown into a comprehensive library of 3D models, HDRIs, and textures — all CC0. The models tend toward realistic props and environmental pieces, but they're high quality and instantly usable.
- ✅ **License:** CC0 (Public Domain)
- 🎯 **Best for:** Realistic 3D assets, environment art, lighting/HDRIs

---

### 4. 🗿 [Sketchfab](https://sketchfab.com)
Sketchfab is a huge repository of 3D models with a large collection of downloadable assets. While many are for sale, there's a substantial number of models available for free. The platform's built-in 3D viewer is a great feature, allowing you to inspect every angle of a model before you download it. Just be sure to check the licensing for each model, as they can vary.
- ✅ **License:** Varies (CC0, CC BY, and others)
- 🎯 **Best for:** Wide variety of styles and categories

---

### 5. 🕹️ [Itch.io](https://itch.io/game-assets/free/tag-3d)
Itch.io is a popular platform for indie game developers, and it has a massive section for game assets. You can find a wide variety of free 3D game assets, from character models to environmental packs, often with very permissive licenses. The community-driven nature of Itch.io means you'll discover unique and creative assets you won't find anywhere else.
- ✅ **License:** Varies per asset
- 🎯 **Best for:** Unique/creative assets, community packs

---

### 6. 🎭 [Mixamo](https://www.mixamo.com) *(by Adobe)*
Mixamo offers **2,000+ free animations** with auto-rigging, making it one of the top sources for character animation assets.
- ✅ **License:** Free with Adobe account
- 🎯 **Best for:** Character animations, rigging

---

### 7. 🏪 [Unity Asset Store (Free Section)](https://assetstore.unity.com)
The Unity Asset Store's free section features **10,000+ Unity-optimized assets** for game development.
- ✅ **License:** Unity-specific license
- 🎯 **Best for:** Unity developers, ready-to-use prefabs

---

### 8. 🌍 [OpenGameArt.org](https://opengameart.org)
OpenGameArt has been around for over a decade and hosts a massive collection of 2D art, 3D models, music, and sound effects — all under open licences like CC0, CC-BY, or GPL.
- ✅ **License:** CC0, CC-BY, GPL
- 🎯 **Best for:** Open-source projects, large variety

---

### 9. 🪨 [Free3D.com](https://free3d.com)
A large number of models on Free3D have a lower polygon count and can be used in games straight away, covering categories like Architecture, Vehicles, Weapons, Animals, Plants, and more.
- ✅ **Formats:** FBX, OBJ, Blend, glTF, and more
- 🎯 **Best for:** Broad category coverage

---

### 10. 💎 [Quixel Megascans](https://quixel.com)
Quixel recently released a final offline version of Quixel Mixer along with the option to download over **800 free Quixel Megascans assets**. Quixel is a pioneer in photogrammetry-based 3D assets, and all assets are scanned from real-world objects using purpose-built hardware.
- ✅ **License:** Free for use (check terms)
- 🎯 **Best for:** Photorealistic, AAA-quality environments

---

## 📋 License Quick Reference

Here's a breakdown of common asset licenses:
- **CC0 (Public Domain):** Use commercially, modify freely, no attribution required
- **CC BY (Attribution):** Use commercially, modify freely, but must credit the creator
- **CC BY-SA:** Use commercially, modify freely, but must credit + share modifications under same license

---

## 💡 Pro Tips
- Consider using a **complete asset pack** to develop your game if possible. Asset packs often include everything you need to create a game world and are a fantastic way to keep your game art looking consistent.
- Choose assets from the **same creator or pack** (e.g., all Quaternius or all Kenney) and don't mix photorealistic and low-poly cartoon styles.
- Always **verify license compatibility** before commercial use.
